title: fix(auth): record an MCP access token as used only after the MCP door admits the call
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XCEYzJzX4FntEsxxQNvdDn1)_

Fixes #31211
Fixes #30949

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`IAuthService` 新增一个可选成员 `recordMcpAccessTokenUse(principal)`。plugin-auth 的 `verifyMcpAccessToken` 不再顺手记「最近使用时间」，只记住自己返回的那个对象；MCP 门口在封禁检查和权限解析都通过之后，才把这个对象交回去记一次。
- 为什么改：被封禁的人，其 AI 助手的每次 MCP 调用都被门口拒绝，但同一小时 `sys_oauth_consent.last_used_at` 仍被写上，管理员在 `GET /admin/authorized-clients?userId=` 里会看到「这一小时用过」。修法是 6 号席在 #30949 上裁定的方案 A（门口唯一拥有「放行」）。
- 风险与回滚：成员可选，没有它的 auth 服务照旧放行；记录本来就在响应之后异步落库、从不抛错，所以不影响调用结果。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts`（门口末尾那一处调用）、`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`（`verifyMcpAccessToken` 与新方法 `recordMcpAccessTokenUse`，WeakMap 只认自己返回的对象）、`packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts`（新成员的契约文字）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/security/resolve-execution-context.test.ts -t 31211`，预期 6 条全过（放行记一次、封禁/503/未验证/转发凭据都不记、缺成员照样放行）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（落地前由 spec 席做契约复审）。

## What changes

- **spec** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts`): `IAuthService` gains one optional member beside `verifyMcpAccessToken`, `recordMcpAccessTokenUse(principal): void`. Its docblock states the split: verifying a token is not admitting the call; the caller calls this once per admitted call, after its last refusal, with the very object the verifier resolved to; the provider records only an object it returned itself; it returns nothing, never throws and never makes the caller wait. The parameter type is derived from the verifier's own result type, so the two cannot drift. `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` lists the member and adds a third "read together" pair (`verifyMcpAccessToken()` / `recordMcpAccessTokenUse()`).
- **plugin-auth producer** (`auth-manager.ts`, `mcp-client-last-use.ts`): `verifyMcpAccessToken` no longer schedules the consent last-use stamp. It puts the principal it returns in a `WeakMap` with the verified token's `iat` (`issuedAtOf`, moved to `mcp-client-last-use.ts` with the `jose` `decodeJwt` read). `recordMcpAccessTokenUse` stamps only an object in that map, then deletes it, so a hand-built principal, a copy, or the same object handed back twice records nothing more. The stamp itself (`McpClientLastUseStamper`, at most one write per consent per hour per process, after the response) is unchanged. The whole member sits in a `try`, so it never throws.
- **runtime reader** (`resolve-execution-context.ts`): the door keeps the verifier's answer in `verifiedTokenPrincipal` only when the ban read does not refuse it, awaits `resolveRequestExecutionContext`, and only then calls `authService?.recordMcpAccessTokenUse?.(verifiedTokenPrincipal)`. So a banned subject, a grant-read outage (503, thrown before that line) and an unverified token all record nothing. A forward credential never sets it: it is the in-process continuation of a call already recorded. The member is reached through the declared, slot-typed `IAuthService` (no cast to an undeclared member).
- **Changeset** `.changeset/31211-mcp-token-use-after-admission.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime` (kind `none` takes `patch`; widening keeps `patch`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3), with both declaration lines and the host note.

Which owner, and why: the door. Seat 6 ruled option A (record 6710928373 on #30949) of the four-axis analysis in report 6710893443: one owner of "admitted", so a refusal added at the door later needs no second edit, and no second ban read anywhere.

## Tests

- **Red first, through the real door** (one-shot rig, not committed: the `rig()` of `mcp-client-last-use.real-engine.test.ts` with a real `AuthManager` over a real SQL engine, a banned `sys_user` row, a consent written by better-auth's adapter, a jwt-plugin token, resolved by runtime `resolveExecutionContext`). Production sources restored to base `fe97d85b`: `banned=true principalKind=guest ... stamp=HOUR_10 writes=1`, `AssertionError: a refused call stamps nothing`, 1 failed | 1 passed. At head: `banned=true principalKind=guest userId=undefined stamp=null writes=0`, `banned=false principalKind=agent ... writes=1`, 2 passed.
- **Door pins** (`resolve-execution-context.test.ts`, new describe `[#31211]`, 6 cases): admitted records exactly once, with the verifier's own object (`toBe`); banned records nothing; a grant-read outage asserts `code` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` + `status` 503 and records nothing; an unverified token records nothing; a forward credential records nothing; an auth service without the member still admits.
- **Producer pins** (`mcp-client-last-use.real-engine.test.ts`, new describe `[#31211]`, 4 cases): verification alone reads and writes no stamp (control: the same token admitted stamps the hour); a hand-built principal and a spread copy record nothing (control: the verifier's object stamps); one object handed back again in a later hour writes nothing more; the member never throws on an unknown or null principal. The 23 existing calls that expected a stamp from `verifyMcpAccessToken` now go through `admittedCall` (verify, then record the returned object), as the door does.
- **Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty; both packages' tests import these sources directly, so no dist leg):
  1. delete the door call: `admitted: recorded exactly once` red (`expected [] to have a length of 1`).
  2. record at verification, before the ban read: admitted (length 2), banned and 503 cases red, 3 failed.
  3. verifier schedules the stamp again: `verification alone reads no stamp` and the hand-built case red.
  4. any object is recorded (`?? {}`): the hand-built case red.
  5. delete the once-only `delete`: `the same object again is not a second admitted call` red (2 vs 1).
- Suites: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test` 235 files, 4187 passed | 10 skipped (VERDICT command-exit 0); runtime `src/security/` + `http-dispatcher.mcp-oauth.test.ts` + `mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts` 15 files, 228 passed, and `resolve-execution-context.test.ts` 53 passed at the head; spec `src/contracts/` 52 files, 475 passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`: exit 0 each (runtime re-run at the head).

## Acceptance notes

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` is hand-written prose (not under `content/docs/references/`); `check:docs` and the other spec artifact gates are green with no regenerated file (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: all 14 artifacts up to date, against a spec dist built with this member).
- A host that calls `AuthManager.verifyMcpAccessToken` itself (outside the runtime door) no longer gets a stamp from verification; the changeset says to call `recordMcpAccessTokenUse` once it admits the call. No such caller exists in this repo (`verifyMcpAccessToken` has one non-test caller, the runtime door).
- Not ablated: the doc and changeset prose (os-dev: docs are not ablated).

## Verification

- First pass reds and their reruns: `check:where-matcher` exit 1 flagged the new door test's table double (no combinator refusal), fixed in `e8c0e991` (it now refuses `$` operators and object values as the neighbouring double does), rerun exit 0. `check:query-options-erasure` exit 124 at a 300 s cap, rerun uncapped exit 0. `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exit 3 on the shallow clone, exit 0 after `git fetch --depth=1 origin 621a4876`.

- At head `e8c0e991` (a test-only commit on top): re-ran `check:where-matcher`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:closed-ceremony-text`, exit 0 each, plus the runtime typecheck.
